profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 5 of 5 mapped in this cluster) is part of Meta's Los Lunas campus in Valencia County, New Mexico, south of Albuquerque. Meta broke ground here in 2016 with an initial $250 million building; a third data center opened in 2020, and Data Center Dynamics reported the campus had grown to seven buildings by 2023, with a two-building, roughly $800 million expansion then under construction, expected to take about three years and intended to support both current products and future AI hardware generations. The Village of Los Lunas has approved industrial revenue bonds to assist the build-out through Meta's Greater Kudu LLC affiliate, part of a financing structure the village has used across multiple expansion phases. On power, Meta and Public Service Company of New Mexico (PNM) marked commercial operation of the Route 66 Solar Facility in July 2022, a 49.5-megawatt, 450-plus-acre solar installation in neighboring Cibola County built by NextEra Energy Resources with more than 150,000 bifacial solar modules, built specifically to help supply renewable power to the Los Lunas data center. Meta's own fact sheet reports more than $2.5 billion invested in the New Mexico campus overall, roughly 400 operational jobs once complete, 1,100 peak skilled-trade construction workers, more than $4.9 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, LEED Gold certification for campus buildings, and a Meta-supported total of 885 megawatts of new renewable energy plus 100 megawatts of battery storage added in New Mexico as part of Meta's global net-zero and 100%-renewable-electricity commitments. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual Los Lunas structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

reading.body:
Meta's Los Lunas campus in Valencia County, New Mexico is a multi-building facility that has grown since initial construction in 2016 to include seven operating buildings as of 2023, with a two-building expansion then under construction that was expected to require three years to complete. Meta does not publish the current building count, total power consumption, or per-building capacity for Los Lunas, so the scale of the campus remains unquantified in operator sources.

The campus has secured dedicated renewable energy supply through the Route 66 Solar Facility, a 49.5-megawatt solar installation in neighboring Cibola County that reached commercial operation in July 2022 and was built by NextEra Energy Resources specifically to supply power to Los Lunas. Meta's disclosed regional commitment includes 885 megawatts of new renewable energy and 100 megawatts of battery storage added across New Mexico as part of its global decarbonization targets. The campus holds LEED Gold certification.

Los Lunas represents the only data center in New Mexico with any published power specification in operator sources, though that specification itself is not per-building or per-campus. No other facility mapped in the state has disclosed megawatt figures, placing this campus at rank 1 of 14 mapped sites in New Mexico by published capacity, with a total of zero published megawatts attributed to the state in this site's database.
